name: Sukuma Wiki (Kenyan Sautéed Collard Greens With Tomatoes and Ginger)

ingredients.name: fresh peeled ginger, finely sliced into matchsticks

instructions.primary_message: Working in batches stack a few stemmed collard leaves on a cutting board, placing the larger leaves at the bottom. Roll the leaves tightly and slice them into thin strips, approximately 1/8 inch wide. (Make sure they are not too thin, as they may clump together during cooking.)
In a large skillet or sauté pan, heat oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add sliced onion and cook until softened and lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes and ginger and season lightly with salt. Cook, stirring often, until tomatoes have released most of their water, about 5 minutes.

Add collards to the pan and season with salt. Cook, lowering the heat as needed to avoid scorching, until collards have softened but retain a vibrant green color and slightly crunchy texture, 8 to 10 minutes. Or, if desired, cook until collards are fully softened and have darkened in color, 15 to 25 minutes total. Season with salt to taste. Serve.

description: Earthy, and deeply satisfying, these lightly sautéed Kenyan collard greens cook in under 30 minutes and pair perfectly with almost any meat, grain, or bread, to round out a full meal.
notes:
Optional substitutions: extra-virgin olive oil → avocado oil

Notes: If you can’t find collard greens, kale is the next best choice. I have used both curly and lacinato kale. They are a bit more finicky to chop due to the shape of their leaves, but they are closer in flavor to the original than other dark leafy greens such as Swiss chard, which is too bitter for this dish.
author: Kiano Moju
